title: Minimum Array Changes to Make Differences Equal
summary: Given an integer array nums of even size n and an integer k, you can replace any element with any integer in the range 0 to k.
statement: Given an integer array nums of even size n and an integer k, you can replace any element with any integer in the range 0 to k. Find the minimum number of changes needed so that the absolute difference between each element and its corresponding element from the end of the array is the same.
constraints: nums has even positive length and every value lies from zero through k.
One change replaces one element by any integer from zero through k.
Make abs(nums[i]-nums[n-1-i]) equal for every mirrored pair using the fewest changes.
hints: For a pair, its current difference costs zero; any target through a computable limit costs one; larger targets cost two.
Start every pair at cost two and apply range-difference savings for its one-change interval and exact current difference.
limit=max(a,b,k-a,k-b); subtract one on [0,limit] and one more at abs(a-b); prefix-scan targets.
The delta events reproduce each pair’s exact 0/1/2 cost function, so minimizing their sum over all targets is optimal.
editorial: The delta events reproduce each pair’s exact 0/1/2 cost function, so minimizing their sum over all targets is optimal.

tests.explanation: Choosing a common difference two lets one pair stay unchanged and fixes the other two with one change each.
Every mirrored difference is already zero, so no changes are needed.
